about.headline: Five years turning commerce requirements into systems that hold
intro: I am Gaurav Kumar, an E-Commerce Specialist and Software Engineer based in Bangalore. For the last five years I have worked almost entirely inside Salesforce Commerce Cloud, on the parts of a storefront where mistakes are expensive: product discovery, cart, checkout, payments and order flow.

That work taught me something narrow but useful. A commerce platform is not really a website. It is a distributed system with a shopping interface attached, and most of the hard problems live in the integrations, the API contracts and the paths users hit under load.

Alongside the e-commerce work I build backend and distributed systems in Java and Spring Boot, and I design for scale rather than for demos. E-commerce is the specialisation. Backend and systems engineering is the range around it.

journey.title: Started in full-stack e-commerce

journey.title: Moved into cart and checkout ownership
journey.description: Joined Merkle (Dentsu) and took on cart architecture, fulfilment options and payment integrations for a US specialty retailer.

journey.title: Led a headless migration

journey.title: Senior Engineer and Commerce Expert
journey.description: At Litmus7, Drove backend development and architecture for a global fashion retailer. Took full ownership of the core commerce solution, implemented secure payment gateways, and redesigned high-traffic PLP and PDP interfaces.

journey.title: Broadened into backend systems at scale
journey.description: Added deep Java, Spring Boot, system design and applied AI engineering capability through a structured software engineering program, aimed at larger-scale SDE work.

principles.title: Understand the constraint before the code
principles.description: Most bad architecture is a correct solution to the wrong problem. I spend the first part of any project finding the real constraint, whether that is latency, a partner API, a migration window or a business rule nobody wrote down.

principles.title: Measure, then optimise
principles.description: Performance work without a baseline is guesswork. I profile the actual path, fix what the numbers point at, and verify the result against the same measurement.

principles.title: Boring architecture scales further
principles.description: Clear service boundaries, predictable data models and well-versioned contracts outlast clever abstractions. I optimise for the engineer who picks this up in two years.

principles.title: Own the path end to end
principles.description: A checkout is not done when the endpoint returns 200. It is done when payments settle, orders export, failures are visible and someone on call can act on them.

principles.title: Write it down
principles.description: Design docs, API contracts and runbooks are part of the deliverable. Documentation is what lets a team move fast without depending on one person's memory.
